artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite point set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$, call a subset $P' \subseteq P$ "distance-distinct" if no positive distance is realized by two different unordered pairs of points of $P'$ (equivalently, the pairwise distances among points of $P'$ are all distinct). Define
\[
 \mathrm{sub}(P) = \max\{|P'| : P' \subseteq P \text{ is distance-distinct}\},
\]
and let
\[
 \mathrm{sub}(n) = \min_{\substack{P \subset \mathbb{R}^2 \\ |P| = n}} \mathrm{sub}(P),
\]
so that $\mathrm{sub}(n)$ is the largest integer such that every $n$-point set in the plane contains a distance-distinct subset of size $\mathrm{sub}(n)$.

It is known that
\[
 \mathrm{sub}(n) = O\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{n}}{(\log n)^{1/4}}\right),
\]
witnessed by a $\sqrt{n} \times \sqrt{n}$ section of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$, and that $\mathrm{sub}(n) = \Omega(n^{1/3}/(\log n)^{1/3})$.

Determine the asymptotic order of $\mathrm{sub}(n)$ as $n \to \infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, posed by Erdős, asks for the asymptotic order of sub(n). The best published bounds remain Ω(n^{1/3}/(log n)^{1/3}) (Charalambides, 2013) and O(√n/(log n)^{1/4}) (from the √n × √n integer lattice via the Erdős–Guy bound on distinct distances). No sharp asymptotic determination appears in the literature, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A note on distinct distance subsets (Charalambides)
status_evidence.snippet: Given a set of N points in the plane, there is a subset of size ≳ (N/log N)^{1/3} with all pairwise distances distinct.
status_evidence.claim: Best known lower bound sub(n) = Ω(n^{1/3}/(log n)^{1/3}).

status_evidence.title: Distinct Distances: Open Problems and Current Bounds
status_evidence.snippet: sub(n) ≤ O(√n/(log n)^{1/4}) via the √n × √n integer lattice; problem listed as open (Erdős).
status_evidence.claim: The asymptotic order of sub(n) is listed as an open problem with the stated upper bound.

status_evidence.title: Point sets with distinct distances (Lefmann–Thiele)
status_evidence.snippet: Any n points in the plane contain a subset of size c·n^{1/4} with distinct mutual distances.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier lower bound improved by later work; the problem of determining the asymptotic order remains.
